ai.definition: Quantum cryptography applications, specifically Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), leverage the unique properties of quantum mechanics to create unbreakable encryption keys for secure data transmission.
ai.howItWorks: QKD works by using single photons to transmit information. Any attempt to intercept or measure these photons disrupts their state, alerting both sender and receiver to potential eavesdropping, thus ensuring the security of the key exchange process.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional cryptographic methods can be compromised through advanced computational attacks. QKD provides a fundamentally secure method for generating encryption keys that are immune to such attacks.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing involves creating single-photon sources and detectors with high precision, often using semiconductor technologies or specialized optical setups.
ai.buildProcess: Components include quantum dots, photonic crystals, and other nanostructured materials. The process is highly complex and requires cleanroom environments.
ai.costDrivers: High material costs for precise components, expensive equipment for production, and the need for low-noise environments contribute to high initial setup costs.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to move from niche applications to broader adoption as technology matures and standards are established.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks are still evolving. Standards bodies like NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) are working on guidelines for QKD implementation.
ai.risks: Technological risks include scaling issues, integration with existing infrastructure, and the need for specialized training. Economic risks involve high initial costs and uncertain market demand.
ai.profitability: Currently limited due to high costs and niche applications but expected to improve as technology matures and economies of scale are achieved.
ai.futureDevelopment: Research is focused on improving efficiency, increasing transmission distances, and developing more practical integration methods with existing communication systems.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and precise control processes.

glossary.def: A method for secure key exchange using the principles of quantum mechanics.
Devices that emit individual photons, crucial for QKD.
Structured materials with a periodic arrangement of dielectrics to control light propagation.

subsystems.name: Transmitter
subsystems.role: prepares and sends the quantum states that carry the key.
parts: quantum random number generator for basis choice

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: carries single photons or entangled pairs between the two parties.

subsystems.name: Detector module
subsystems.role: measures the received states in a randomly chosen basis.
parts: single-photon detectors (InGaAs avalanche photodiodes or superconducting nanowire detectors)

subsystems.name: Classical authenticated channel
subsystems.role: lets both sides compare bases, correct errors and compress the key without an eavesdropper altering messages.

subsystems.name: Post-processing
subsystems.role: turns raw correlated bits into a secret key.

subsystems.name: Key management and network layer
subsystems.role: stores keys and feeds them to encrypting equipment.
parts: interfaces to AES or one-time-pad encryptors

buildSteps.title: Design the link
buildSteps.detail: Choose fibre or free-space, measure the loss over the route, and set a key-rate target that detectors and error correction can meet.

buildSteps.title: Build the transmitter
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a laser, modulator, attenuator and encoder so each pulse contains on average far less than one photon.

buildSteps.title: Build the receiver
buildSteps.detail: Install single-photon detectors, a random basis selector and timing electronics in a temperature-controlled enclosure.

buildSteps.title: Lay or point the channel
buildSteps.detail: Use a dedicated dark fibre pair between the sites, or align a telescope link for free-space or satellite QKD.

buildSteps.title: Authenticate the classical channel
buildSteps.detail: Load a pre-shared secret or a post-quantum signature key so the basis-sifting messages cannot be spoofed.

buildSteps.title: Run the protocol
buildSteps.detail: Transmit quantum states, record detections, then publicly compare bases to keep only matching events.

buildSteps.title: Extract a secret key
buildSteps.detail: Correct remaining errors and apply privacy amplification to shrink any eavesdropper's knowledge to a negligible amount.

buildSteps.title: Deliver keys to encryptors
buildSteps.detail: Feed the fresh key to AES or a one-time pad for data in transit, and log key consumption.

buildSteps.title: Extend reach with trusted nodes
buildSteps.detail: Where single-link distance is too short, chain links through secure intermediate nodes that decrypt and re-encrypt.

prerequisites.why: they must catch individual photons with low noise; superconducting types are fast but need cryogenics.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss optical fibre and free-space optics
prerequisites.why: loss limits both distance and key rate, since photons cannot be copied or amplified.
basis and bit choices must be unpredictable, not merely pseudo-random.
without authentication, a man-in-the-middle can impersonate either side; post-quantum signatures are the scalable fix.
they would allow long-distance entanglement without trusted nodes, which no deployed system can yet do.
they promise lower cost and mass production, but are still maturing.

pathway.milestone: point-to-point and metro QKD links, plus satellite demonstrations such as Micius (2016) and the Beijing–Shanghai backbone (2017)
pathway.unlocks: high-value links where a dedicated fibre and trusted nodes are acceptable.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale QKD integrated into telecom equipment, with higher key rates and automated key management
pathway.unlocks: cheaper deployment in data-centre and enterprise networks.

pathway.milestone: routine satellite QKD and intercontinental key relay
pathway.unlocks: key distribution between continents where no fibre exists.
device-independent security and a path toward a quantum internet.
